config.title: Star Rating Component

intro.title: Star Rating Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive Star Rating component that allows users to select and display a rating from one to five stars. You will learn how to manage component state in React to track the current rating and hover state for visual feedback. The lesson will involve using TypeScript for type safety, handling click and mouse events, and conditionally rendering CSS classes to fill stars. By the end, you'll have a reusable UI component that demonstrates fundamental React patterns like state management and event handling.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are ubiquitous in modern web applications where user feedback and content quality assessment are essential. You'll find them in e-commerce platforms like Amazon and eBay where customers rate products, in streaming services like Netflix and Hulu for content reviews, and in marketplace apps like Airbnb and Uber for service provider ratings. As a developer, you'll implement these interactive UI elements in product detail pages, review sections, and feedback forms to capture user sentiment and display aggregated ratings. Mastering this component prepares you for building intuitive rating systems that enhance user engagement across various application types.

objectives: Implement a reusable StarRating component using TypeScript interfaces
Define a fixed array of star placeholders and map it to JSX elements
Initialize and manage the rating state with React hooks
Render interactive star icons based on the current rating value
Configure click handlers to update the rating when stars are selected
Manipulate the UI to display both filled and empty star states
Apply conditional styling to visually represent the selected rating
Integrate the component into a parent application with proper props binding

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' module.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Define the StarRating component and its props interface
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StarRating and define an interface for its props with a maxRating property of type number.
steps.hint: Declare the interface first, then add a component named StarRating — either `function StarRating(…) { }` or `const StarRating = (…) => { }`. Type the parameter with `StarRatingProps` when you add the signature (e.g. `(props: StarRatingProps)` or `({ maxRating }: StarRatingProps)`). An empty body is fine for this step.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define StarRating component and props interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a StarRating component function and a props interface with maxRating: number.
successCriteria: StarRating component is defined as a function and accepts props typed with an interface containing maxRating: number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created both the interface for props and the StarRating component function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined an interface for props with maxRating: number and created a StarRating component function.

steps.title: Initialize rating state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your StarRating component, declare a state variable named 'rating' and its setter using useState, initializing it to 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the initial value (0) and destructure the returned array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state for a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'rating' initialized to 0, ready to track the user's selected rating.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'rating' and its setter, initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState to declare both the state variable and its setter, and initialize it to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState to create a state variable named 'rating' with an initial value of 0.

steps.title: Create the handleStarClick handler
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component, define a function named handleStarClick that takes a star index (number) as a parameter and updates the rating state to that index.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives a star index and calls setRating with that index value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleStarClick function that updates the rating state when called with a star index.
successCriteria: A function named handleStarClick is defined, takes a number parameter, and calls setRating with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure handleStarClick takes a number parameter and calls setRating with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleStarClick function isn't defined correctly. It should take a star index and update the rating state.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: In your StarRating component, return a div element with the class name 'star-rating'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return value (null) with a JSX div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div container with the class 'star-rating', providing a root element for the star rating UI.
successCriteria: The component returns a JSX div element with className='star-rating'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element with the exact class name 'star-rating'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='star-rating'. Check that you've replaced 'null' with the correct JSX.

steps.title: Define a stars array with five labels
steps.instruction: Inside **StarRating**, **above** the `return`, declare **`const stars`** as an array of **five** strings — e.g. **`'star1'`**, **`'star2'`**, **`'star3'`**, **`'star4'`**, and **`'star5'`**. Each entry is a stand-in for one star slot; you will **`.map`** over this array in the next step to render the UI.
steps.hint: Use an array literal: `const stars = ['star1', 'star2', 'star3', 'star4', 'star5'];` Place it after your hooks/handlers and before the `return`.
steps.analogousExample:
// Five placeholder labels for five UI slots:
const tabs = ['home', 'profile', 'settings', 'help', 'logout'];
steps.expectedOutcome: A `stars` constant holds exactly five string elements (e.g. star1 … star5), ready to drive rendering in the next step.
successCriteria: `const stars` (or equivalent) declares an array of five strings such as 'star1' through 'star5'.
The array is defined inside the component, before the return.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Good — you have a fixed five-item list to map over next.
steps.feedbackPartial: Define `stars` as an array of five strings (star1 … star5) inside the component, above the return.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add: `const stars = ['star1', 'star2', 'star3', 'star4', 'star5'];` before the return statement.

steps.title: Map over the stars array to create star elements
steps.instruction: Inside the **`star-rating`** container `div`, use **`.map`** on your **`stars`** array. For each item, return a **`span`** element. Use the **loop index** as React’s **`key`** (e.g. `key={index}`).
steps.hint: Pattern: `{stars.map((star, index) => ( ... ))}`. You will fill the span content in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each entry in `stars` produces one `span` in the DOM, keyed by index.
successCriteria: `.map` is called on the `stars` array inside the container div.
Each mapped element is a `span` with a stable `key` derived from the index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use `stars.map((star, index) => ...)` inside the div and return a `<span key={index}>` for each row.

steps.title: Display star character and apply conditional styling
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, make each span display a star character (★) and conditionally apply an 'active' class if the star index is less than or equal to the current rating.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally add the 'active' class to the className attribute based on the index and rating comparison.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star span will show a filled star character (★) and have an 'active' class when its index is less than or equal to the current rating, enabling visual styling.
successCriteria: The span displays ★ and conditionally includes className='active' based on index <= rating.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each span shows ★ and conditionally adds the 'active' class when index <= rating.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the map callback: each span should contain ★ and conditionally apply the 'active' class based on the rating comparison.

steps.title: Wire onClick to handleStarClick
steps.instruction: Add an onClick handler to each star span that calls handleStarClick with the appropriate star index.
steps.hint: The index parameter for each star is available in the map callback. Pass it to handleStarClick when the star is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a click handler
<button onClick={() => handleClick(index)}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star span will have an onClick handler that triggers handleStarClick with the correct star index when clicked.
successCriteria: The onClick handler is added to each star span and correctly calls handleStarClick with the star's index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding onClick to the span element and passing the correct index to handleStarClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onClick handler is missing or incorrectly implemented. Check that you're adding it to the span and calling handleStarClick with the index.

steps.title: Add a reset button
steps.instruction: After the stars mapping, add a button element with the text 'Reset' and an onClick handler that sets the rating state back to 0.
steps.hint: Place the button after the closing of the `stars.map(...)` expression. Use setRating(0) inside the onClick handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a reset button
<button onClick={() => setValue(0)}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Reset' button appears below the stars. Clicking it resets the rating to 0.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Reset' is added after the stars, and its onClick handler calls setRating(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a reset button that clears the rating.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure its onClick handler correctly resets the rating to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or not properly configured. Add a button with text 'Reset' and an onClick handler that sets rating to 0.

steps.title: Display the current rating text
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the star container that displays the current rating value in the format 'Rating: X/5' where X is the rating state value.
steps.hint:
Place a

tag after the star container div and use curly braces to embed the rating state value in the text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph that updates dynamically as the rating changes, displaying the current rating value out of the maximum stars.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that displays the current rating value in the format 'Rating: X/5' where X is the rating state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the rating state value in the correct format (e.g., 'Rating: 3/5').
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the rating state value correctly. Try adding

Rating: {rating}/{maxStars}

after the star container.
